conditionDescription: Each agent's prompt, round brief and read_negotiation tool show the counterparty's offers from earlier rounds, as a public chain or plain commit-reveal would.
harness: Local Hardhat network, in-process, fresh per run: vendored ERC-8004 registries, ReputationGate and SealedNegotiation deployed by scripts/leak-experiment.ts, reputation seeded as scripts/seed-demo.ts did on Monad testnet. Not a field study.
terms: Demo: price per 1,000 calls to a market-data API, 30-day term, in US cents
disclosure: Throwaway local chain: mandates, offers, notes and salts are published so the run can be audited.

buyer.explanation: Opened at 3450, 550 below the reference, 850 below its limit.
buyer.note: PLAN (3 rounds): R1 anchor low at 3450 (-550 vs ref 4000), well under my 4300 limit, to pull the midpoint down. R2: read seller's number; if they drop toward 4000-4200, step up to ~3800-3900 (concede, but keep gap); if they stay high/ stubborn above 4600, only move to ~3700 and signal firmness. R3: final step to at most 4150-4200 — NEVER submit 4300, since a number at the limit reveals my principal's ceiling and weakens future deals. Accept a crossing midpoint up to ~4150; a deal at/below 4200 b

seller.explanation: Opened at 5400, 1400 above the reference, 1300 above its limit.
seller.note:
PLAN: I'm the seller; my floor is 4100 (hard limit, never submit below, and avoid landing exactly on 4100 so the buyer doesn't learn my reservation price). Reference is 4000, so I need the buyer to move up above it.
R1: open at 5400 (+1400 vs reference) — high enough to have 2 credible concession steps, low enough to stay believable.
R2: if no cross, step down to ~4700 (roughly half the gap), and react to the buyer's R1/R2 numbers: if the buyer is climbing fast (e.g. already 4300+), concede less
